doc.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Europe, Los Angeles and the Legrand break
title: Meeting Jill Goodwin and driving east
summary: His marriage to Chan unravels, he meets Jill, they drive to New York, and he gets the Legrand call.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: club wanted me, you know. They heard that I was in town so I gave them a pretty stiff price. I mean, I was used to five years in Europe, you know, I wasn’t going to work for scale. And I remember the club owner saying, “Stay here long enough, we’ll get you to for scale,” and I said, “I’m out of here,” you know. And by that point my marriage to Chan was kind of on the rocks, and I met Jill, and fell in love with Jill, my present wife, Jill Goodwin, who happens to be my, the sister of my drummer, Bill Goodwin.
Who, I think, is one of the great drummers.
Yeah, he is. He plays a song.
I think he’s one of the great drummers.
Yeah, I think you’re right. I think Steve Gilmore is one of the great bass players. We’ve been together thirty five years, which is another whole story.

[Phil says to his cat] Stop. [Chuckles] That’s my cat. [MN laughs] So, it’s all part of the woof and web of [chuckles] Yeah, so I said, “I gotta get out of here,” and Jill said, “Well, I want to get out of here too.” She was coming off a divorce also. We were both, you know, single and looking to go to the east coast, so. I was actually heading back to Europe since my return to America hadn’t worked out. The year I was in L.A. I made three thousand dollars in that year, you know. I used to make more than that in a night in Europe with my own band. So I, I was going back to France, [coughs] I thought. But you know we drove to New York uh I gave her a ride. And she went and stayed with Chuck Israels who was a good friend of hers, and I went on to, I stayed with Jerry Dodgion. uh And he got a call from uh Michel Legrand’s manager who said, “Jerry, I got Eddie Daniels for the first week, Michel is doing an album in the second week and we need a good player.” And Jerry said, “Well I’m working but Phil Woods is here. You want to talk to him?” He said, “Phil? Oh yeah sure.” So I got the gig to play with Michel Legrand the second week at uh Live, we did an album called Live at Jimmy’s. I played uh “You Must Believe in Spring” and at that time Jill had hepititis and I didn’t know what my divorce was going to happen. I mean, I was, I didn’t know where I was going to live and the record won a, led to a forming of a company called Griffin
